models_evaluated: LoRA fine-tuned LLM (single-site, sequential multi-site, joint)

links.outcome: Micro F1 of locally fine-tuned LoRA models versus an untuned 70B model for mobility extraction
links.effect: Sequential fine-tuning F1 0.861 and joint 0.894 for extraction; 0.912 and 0.900 for impairment classification; both outperformed the untuned 70B model.
links.quote: Both sequential and joint fine-tuning outperformed an untuned 70B model.

links.outcome: Cross-site generalization of single-site fine-tuned models across 3 institutions
links.effect: Single-site LoRA models showed robust cross-site generalization; no numbers reported in the abstract.
links.quote: Additionally, single-site LoRA models showed robust cross-site generalization.

unlisted_practices: Sequential multi-site fine-tuning that transfers only LoRA weights between sites, avoiding pooling of patient data, compared with centralized joint fine-tuning

screen.reason: Evaluates sequential multi-site fine-tuning (federated-style weight transfer) as an incremental deployment and adaptation practice across institutions to preserve data privacy compared to pooled joint training.
